podcast.body: A radio hit on alt-rock stations in 1990, this song is characterized by its existentialist themes, encouraging listeners to "bend your head around existentialist things" to fully grasp its meaning. It contributed to Billboard eventually labeling the band "Nerd Rock Kings." "Yes, a radio hit on alt rock stations in 1990. They might be giants and particle man."

podcast.body: Featured on their 1990 album `Flood`, "Particle Man" became a big alternative song that year. Although not originally intended as such, it was widely adopted by elementary school teachers and taught to children. "They might be giants with Particle Man from 1990, big alternative song that year. In fact, Particle Man was picked up by elementary school teachers everywhere and taught to kids."

podcast.body: This song became an alt-rock radio hit in 1990, known for its existentialist themes that defy straightforward interpretation. It showcased They Might Be Giants' quirky and intellectual songwriting, making it a prominent example of their nerdy appeal. "It's called Particle Man. And don't try to make sense of this unless you bend your head around existentialist things. Otherwise, you're just going to hurt yourself."
